seo.metaDescription: Trends over time with a clear line between what happened and what is expected: solid actuals, a dashed forecast and a target that stays on the chart.

props.markdown: Trends over time with a clear line between what happened and what is expected. Actual values are solid, a forecast is dashed, and a target stays on the chart.

Use `LineChart` for a handful of series that share an x axis: revenue against plan, a forecast that continues the actuals, a scenario next to the current path. For a single value per period, `BarChart` usually reads faster.

`underlay` takes marks that sit under the lines, such as an `<Area>` on a time axis. The chart draws in a fixed order: the grid first, then the `underlay`, then the `target` and `band`, then the series, then the axes, and last your `children`. So an `underlay` is above the grid and under every line, and `children` stay above the lines. Here last year's orders are a soft area behind this year's line. The `underlay` is a plain element, so every prop of this chart is still serializable.

`LineChart` is built on `Chart`, so it follows the same keyboard model as the other charts: it is a single tab stop, and tabbing in shows the first point with its tooltip and announces it. A click that focuses the chart does not. `←` and `→` (and `↑` and `↓`) move to the previous or next point, and `Home` and `End` jump to the first and last. `Enter` or `Space` selects the active point when the chart has `onSelect`, but only a point that can be selected (a point with `selectable: false` never promises `Enter`). `Esc` clears the active point; it is only consumed when a point is active, so an enclosing dialog still closes.

The widget’s description ends with a keyboard hint (“Use arrow keys to move between points, Home and End for first and last, Escape to clear.”, plus “Press Enter to select.” with `onSelect`). `keyboardHint` replaces it, for example to translate it, and `keyboardHint=""` turns it off.

Screen readers get the chart title and description, then an announcement for each point the keyboard moves to: the position, the x and each series’ value, such as “9 of 9, Dec, 36.0% on the current path, 37.6% with changes”. A visually hidden data table follows the chart with every value, and `dataTable` renames its caption and headers or turns it off. The `underlay` is drawing only: it is hidden from assistive technology like the rest of the SVG, so put what it shows in the `description` or the data, as the example does with last year’s orders.
The full model is in the [accessibility guide](https://github.com/mwadon/tally-charts/blob/main/docs/a11y.md).
